stem: Priya takes a loan of Rs 12,000 at 8% per annum compounded half-yearly. What amount does she owe at the end of 1 year? [Given: (1.04)^2 = 1.0816]

per_option_rationale.rationale: When compounding is more frequent than annual, you must divide the rate and multiply the periods before plugging in; using the annual rate directly gives a wrong (lower) answer.
Rs 12,960 = 12000 x 1.08 applies the annual rate 8% as if compounding were annual (n = 1 period), ignoring the half-yearly conversion to 4% per half-year over 2 periods.
Rs 13,056 = 12000 x (1 + 0.08/2)^4 mistakenly uses n = 4 half-years for a 1-year loan; the borrower doubled the number of periods.
Rs 12,998.40 arises from computing 12000 x 1.0832 instead of 1.0816; an arithmetic slip where (1.04)^2 was incorrectly evaluated as 1.0832.

explanation: Half-yearly compounding: rate per period = 8%/2 = 4%; periods = 1 x 2 = 2. A = 12000 x (1.04)^2 = 12000 x 1.0816 = Rs 12,979.20.

explanation_sections.punchline: When compounding is more frequent than annual, you must divide the rate and multiply the periods before plugging in; using the annual rate directly gives a wrong (lower) answer.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: A = P x (1 + r/m)^(n*m). P = 12000, r = 0.08, m = 2 (half-yearly), n = 1 year. So periodic rate = 0.04, periods = 2. A = 12000 x (1.04)^2 = 12000 x 1.0816 = 12979.20.
explanation_sections.lesson: The conversion rule is: r_period = r_annual / m and total_periods = n x m. Always perform this two-step conversion before applying the CI formula.
explanation_sections.timing: 75 seconds: identify m = 2, compute 12000 x 1.0816. Trap is option 2 (annual rate applied directly, giving 12960); it is the most common wrong answer.
